short_answer: Larry Ness was a real and well known handicapper. He was on Proline, the USA Network handicapping show, and on Wayne Root's Winning Edge, and he sold picks for decades through his own service and later through online pick sites. Gambling911 reported on 7 Sep 2022 that he had died at 68.
We found no Larry Ness package for sale on 16 Nov 2026. If you see his name on a sales page today, ask who is making the picks.

Whether his picks made money over his career is something nobody can now check. We found no full, time stamped log of his picks, and his best known credential, a 1985 Castaways contest win, was publicly disputed by another handicapper in 2022. Forum opinion over 15 years is split about evenly.

guarantee: We found no guarantee terms for Larry Ness, because we found no current sales page. Any guarantee he offered in the past would have been set by the site selling his picks.
As with every pick service, losses on the bets themselves are never covered, and they are usually far larger than any package price.

claims_note: The 1985 contest claim is the clearest problem. Three days after his death, Gambling911 published a veteran handicapper's account that he, not Ness, made the picks for that winning entry, which he says was entered as Top Play Sports with Jim Feist paying the fee, and that Ness was a paid front man. Ness could not respond, and Gambling911 said the question was "to be determined." We found no follow up.
The kind words in the obituary and eulogy come from friends and business partners. They are fair to report, but they are not a record.
record: What a buyer can verify independently: nothing that we could find. We found no full, time stamped log of every Larry Ness pick, no audited monitor record we could open, and no court or regulator record about him.

What was said publicly: a 2007 TheRX member posted a 162-82 record for that year without a source, and a 2022 Sportsbook Review member noted that his last listed pick, a White Sox bet, won. Neither is a full record.

customers_intro: Independent comment on Larry Ness comes from three forum threads, one from 2007 and two written the week he died in 2022. None includes a receipt or a full record. Below is what we found and how much weight it can carry.

customers.text: We read about 30 opinion posts across three threads on TheRX, Covers and Sportsbook Review, from 2007 and 2022. Opinion splits close to evenly. Supporters say he was respected, did his own research, bet his own money and had good stretches. Critics say his records could not be checked because his site kept no archive, that he was a name on the label rather than the person picking, and that his biggest plays were worth betting against. Several posts are general complaints about all touts rather than about him. Nobody in these threads posted a receipt or a season of results from buying his picks, and our Reddit archive search found no post about him.

In a TheRX thread about his plays, one member called him one of the biggest frauds in the business and said to bet against him, and another claimed he did not pick the games himself and that his name was what sold. Neither gave evidence.
In the same thread, other members called him a good handicapper who picks winners, said he was having a great year, and one posted a 162-82 record for the year without a source.

One member said his recent results looked good but that his website had no archive of past picks, so he would not buy. Another said he bet a lot of favorites but had only three losing weeks in sixteen.

On Sportsbook Review the week he died, one member said a profile calling him honest could not be verified but matched his reputation, and described him as someone who researched his picks and bet his own money. Another called him a respected figure in the business.
In the same thread, one member doubted he was ever a sharp or winning bettor, but credited his convincing on air style.

On Covers, one member said he profited for years by betting against Ness's top plays and called him a scammer, and another described his handicapping as mediocre at best. A third member in the same thread called him one of the best handicappers. None gave records.
We found no current Larry Ness sales page. The Reddit archive post search for r/sportsbook found no post about him.

conflicts: The most generous accounts of his career come from Wayne Root, his longtime business partner, and from a pick site profile. They are fair to report but not independent.
The 1985 contest claim that appeared on sales pages was disputed by another handicapper who says he made the picks for that entry. The dispute was never settled in anything we found.
strengths: A real, documented career on national handicapping TV and radio over two decades.
Some independent forum members describe him as respected and as someone who bet his own picks.
concerns: Reported dead since Sep 2022. Any product sold under his name today would be made by someone else.
No full public record of his picks was ever found, and one 2007 forum member said his site kept no archive.
His headline contest credential is publicly disputed.
Forum opinion is split, and the negative posts include allegations that he fronted for picks made by others. These are allegations without evidence.
checklist: If any site sells picks under the Larry Ness name, ask who makes them and when that person started.
Ask any seller for every pick from the last 12 months with the line, the odds and the time it was sent. A list of hot runs is not a record.
Read the guarantee for the words refund, credit and extension. Most "guarantees" in this business are credits.
Write down each pick yourself the moment you receive it, with the line you can actually get.
Give any handicapper a few hundred picks before you call them a winner. Short runs swing hard both ways.
faq: He was a real, long running TV handicapper who sold picks for decades. Gambling911 reported he died in Sep 2022, and we found no current Larry Ness package for sale. We could not verify his long run record, and we found no court or regulator action involving him.
How much does Larry Ness cost?
We found no current price. No sales page under his name was live on 16 Nov 2026.
Does Larry Ness have a verified record?
No. We found no full, time stamped record of his picks, and his 1985 Castaways contest win was disputed by another handicapper in 2022.
What do bettors say about Larry Ness?

Opinion is split. Some forum members called him respected and said he bet his own picks; others called him a front man or said his top plays were worth fading. Nobody we found posted a full record either way.
